A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CQ-DINO and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting comparison. The complete v3 Appendix A was inspected; v1 ends with references and contains no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original CQ-DINO detection results on V3Det and COCO, alongside component ablations, gradient measurements and scalability experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports additional quantitative component controls and training-gradient results in Appendix A.2.

M1.justification: Both versions retain CLIP-initialized category queries, image-guided selection, hierarchical or self-attention correlation encoding, the GroundingDINO-based detection components, identical losses and two-stage training. Rewording and diagram revisions do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Actual training and evaluation coverage remains V3Det and COCO, with the same backbone pretraining variants. Open Images is added only to related work; the new gradient analysis uses existing experimental coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark, generative-detector and focal-loss comparisons retain their comparator sets. The no-selection variants already appeared as out-of-memory rows in v1, and the new gradient diagnostic reuses previously compared default and tuned DINO configurations.

E3.justification: v3 Section 4.3 uses eight H800-80G GPUs to evaluate no-selection controls that failed on A100-40G hardware in v1. Appendix A.2 also introduces a gradient-norm diagnostic across training. Standard benchmark splits, backbones, batch size and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 Table 4 replaces v1 Table 3's out-of-memory-only controls with quantitative experiments testing the central selection module's accuracy and efficiency contribution. New Appendix A.2/Figure 6 examines gradient dynamics against default and tuned DINO. The query-count and backbone-dependent focal-loss studies are retained and relocated, not newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Figure 6's scatter and discussion of variance concern fluctuations during training, rather than uncertainty estimated across independent runs.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–2 are unchanged. Fine-tuned GenerateU's AP/AP50/AP75 changes from 17.2/22.4/17.7 to 21.8/27.2/22.1. New no-selection controls report 47.3 and 49.4 AP; ablation FPS values are revised under changed hardware. Figure 6 adds gradient-norm findings, and the focal-loss discussion corrects 47.2 to the already-tabulated 47.4 AP. These are localized additions and revisions, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: After Equation 3, v3 explicitly conditions the gradient-ratio argument on average negative activation remaining non-negligible during early training. This qualifies the mathematical reasoning; Equations 1–7 otherwise remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain diagnosing gradient dilution, encoding category correlations and selecting relevant categories per image. Both abstracts claim a 2.1-point AP advantage on V3Det and competitive COCO performance; the revised conclusion does not materially expand these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 newly interprets moderate, stable gradient norms as evidence of improved optimization. The limitations discussion qualifies the earlier categorical dismissal of a recall bottleneck using the retained query-count results, and describes possible coordination problems between training stages more explicitly.

D1.justification: v3 discloses H800 hardware for the component controls and an approximately one-hour first training stage. The abstract changes a promised dataset/code release to a statement that code is available at the same repository. This is a changed availability statement, not independently verified access.

R1.justification: v3 adds Open Images but removes the LVIS long-tail discussion and citations covering Equalization/SeeSaw losses, 11k-class detection and Detic, among others. This narrows relevant background while retaining the principal positioning against classification-head, text-prompted and generative detectors.

P1.justification: Extensive introduction and related-work rewriting accompanies structural changes: detector families are consolidated under Section 2.2, datasets and implementation details are merged, and existing sensitivity studies move into Appendix A. Terminology and the author list also change.

P2.justification: The document switches from two-column to single-column formatting, relocates Figure 1 and numerous tables, redraws and rearranges method diagrams, and places Figures 4–5 side by side. The component table is reformatted and Figure 6 is added, producing substantial visual reorganization beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The completed no-selection controls and new gradient diagnostics strengthen empirical support for the central mechanism. The corrected focal-loss value and more qualified recall discussion also improve clarity. These gains are limited by reduced coverage of relevant gradient-balancing literature and the unexplained GenerateU score revision; the principal method and benchmark findings remain stable.
